class: Frame: an ask-first heading over a warfarin order and a metformin order, which may make the patient ask before taking either.
Frame: a parenthesized ask-first note after the warfarin line, which may read as a condition on taking it.
Frame: a have-you-questions heading over an as-needed acetaminophen order and a scheduled metformin order, which may leave the patient unsure whether to take the first.
Frame: a read-carefully heading over a once-a-week warfarin order and a twice-daily metformin order, which may read the weekly order as routine.
Punctuation: the as-needed frequency of an acetaminophen order printed inside quotation marks, which may read as a phrase quoted from a label rather than the order.
Layout: the as-needed frequency of an acetaminophen order printed inside parentheses after the route, which may read as an optional part of the dose.
Completeness: the list frame over one active metformin order while a warfarin order is a prohibition (doNotPerform true) that the text does not mention.
